def category_match(
    pattr_category: Union[Tuple[AttrCategory, ...], AttrCategory],
    target_category: AttrCategory,
) -> bool:
    """Return True if target_category is this attribute's category.

    Categories are normalized to a tuple of every category the attribute
    belongs to (detailed and general). Match against the whole tuple: the
    primary category lives at index 0, so slicing it off drops plain
    properties, methods, descriptors and anything else with a single tag.
    """
    if pattr_category == target_category:
        return True
    return isinstance(pattr_category, tuple) and target_category in pattr_category

def attr_category_postprocess(get_attr_category_func):
    """Unifies attr_category to a tuple, add AttrCategory.SLOT if needed."""
    @functools.wraps(get_attr_category_func)
    def wrapped(
        name: str, attr: Any, obj: Any
    ) -> Tuple[AttrCategory, ...]:
        category = get_attr_category_func(name, attr, obj)
        category = list(category) if isinstance(category, tuple) else [category]
        # Slot is orthogonal: keep any categories already returned and tag SLOT
        # once. member_descriptor handling may have added it already.
        if is_slotted_attr(obj, name) and AttrCategory.SLOT not in category:
            category.append(AttrCategory.SLOT)
        return tuple(category)

    return wrapped


@attr_category_postprocess
def get_attr_category(
    name: str, attr: Any, obj: Any
) -> Union[Tuple[AttrCategory, ...], AttrCategory]:
    def is_descriptor(candidate: Any) -> bool:
        # Descriptor protocol looks up __get__/__set__/__delete__ on the type,
        # not the instance. hasattr(instance, ...) is wrong for objects whose
        # __getattr__ invents attributes (and would mislabel plain values).
        candidate_type = type(candidate)
        return (
            hasattr(candidate_type, '__get__')
            or hasattr(candidate_type, '__set__')
            or hasattr(candidate_type, '__delete__')
        )

    method_descriptor = type(list.append)
    wrapper_descriptor = type(object.__init__)
    classmethod_descriptor = type(dict.__dict__['fromkeys'])

    if name in ATTR_MAP_CONDITIONAL:
        return ATTR_MAP_CONDITIONAL[name](obj)

    if name in ATTR_MAP:
        return ATTR_MAP[name]

    if inspect.isclass(attr):
        return (
            AttrCategory.EXCEPTION
            if issubclass(attr, Exception)
            else AttrCategory.CLASS
        )
    elif isinstance(attr, staticmethod):
        return (
            AttrCategory.DESCRIPTOR,
            AttrCategory.STATIC_METHOD,
            AttrCategory.FUNCTION,
        )
    elif (
        inspect.isfunction(attr)
        or inspect.ismethod(attr)
        or inspect.isbuiltin(attr)
        or isinstance(
            attr,
            (
                method_descriptor,
                wrapper_descriptor,
                classmethod_descriptor,
                classmethod,
            ),
        )
    ):
        # Technically these are descriptors, but they act as functions.
        # classmethod objects (getattr_static) and classmethod_descriptor
        # (dict.fromkeys) must not fall through to the property bucket.
        return AttrCategory.FUNCTION
    elif inspect.ismemberdescriptor(attr):
        # Slot member descriptors are data attributes, not user descriptors.
        # Tag both so the properties filter and the slot listing agree.
        return AttrCategory.PROPERTY, AttrCategory.SLOT
    elif inspect.isgetsetdescriptor(attr) or isinstance(attr, property):
        # Builtin getset attributes (int.real) and @property are data, not
        # user-defined descriptors.
        return AttrCategory.PROPERTY
    elif is_descriptor(attr):
        # User-defined descriptor. Also a property so data filters keep it.
        return AttrCategory.DESCRIPTOR, AttrCategory.PROPERTY
    else:
        # attr that is neither function nor class is a normal variable,
        # and it's classified to property.
        return AttrCategory.PROPERTY

    """Unifies attr_category to a tuple, add AttrCategory.SLOT if needed."""
    @functools.wraps(get_attr_category_func)
    def wrapped(
        name: str, attr: Any, obj: Any
    ) -> Tuple[AttrCategory, ...]:
        category = get_attr_category_func(name, attr, obj)
        category = list(category) if isinstance(category, tuple) else [category]
        if is_slotted_attr(obj, name):
            # Refactoring all tuples to lists is not easy
            # and pleasant. Maybe do this in future if necessary
            category.append(AttrCategory.SLOT)
        return tuple(category)

    return wrapped


@attr_category_postprocess
def get_attr_category(
    name: str, attr: Any, obj: Any
) -> Union[Tuple[AttrCategory, ...], AttrCategory]:
    def is_descriptor(obj: Any) -> bool:
        return (
            hasattr(obj, '__get__')
            or hasattr(obj, '__set__')
            or hasattr(obj, '__delete__')
        )

    method_descriptor = type(list.append)

    if name in ATTR_MAP_CONDITIONAL:
        return ATTR_MAP_CONDITIONAL[name](obj)

    if name in ATTR_MAP:
        return ATTR_MAP[name]

    if inspect.isclass(attr):
        return (
            AttrCategory.EXCEPTION
            if issubclass(attr, Exception)
            else AttrCategory.CLASS
        )
    elif (
        inspect.isfunction(attr)
        or inspect.ismethod(attr)
        or inspect.isbuiltin(attr)
        or isinstance(attr, method_descriptor)
    ):
        # Technically, method_descriptor is descriptor, but since they
        # act as functions, let's treat them as functions.
        return AttrCategory.FUNCTION
    elif isinstance(attr, staticmethod):
        return (
            AttrCategory.DESCRIPTOR,
            AttrCategory.STATIC_METHOD,
            AttrCategory.FUNCTION,
        )
    elif is_descriptor(attr):
        # member_descriptor (slots) and other descriptors are data
        # attributes: both DESCRIPTOR and PROPERTY. SLOT is appended later.
        return AttrCategory.DESCRIPTOR, AttrCategory.PROPERTY
    else:
        # attr that is neither function nor class is a normal variable,
        # and it's classified to property.
        return AttrCategory.PROPERTY

# Detailed category should have larger values than general category.

def category_match(
    pattr_category: Union[Tuple[AttrCategory, ...], AttrCategory],
    target_category: AttrCategory,
) -> bool:
    """Return True if the attribute belongs to target_category.

    Categories are a tuple whose first item is the primary one. Filters such
    as properties, methods and descriptor must see that item too — otherwise
    a bare PROPERTY/FUNCTION never matches, and DESCRIPTOR is invisible when
    it sits in front of PROPERTY. Only dunder names, which store PROPERTY in
    a later slot, used to show up.
    """
    if pattr_category == target_category:
        return True
    return isinstance(pattr_category, tuple) and target_category in pattr_category

        return (
            hasattr(obj, '__get__')
            or hasattr(obj, '__set__')
            or hasattr(obj, '__delete__')

    if name in ATTR_MAP_CONDITIONAL:

    if inspect.isclass(attr):

            AttrCategory.EXCEPTION
            if issubclass(attr, Exception)
            else AttrCategory.CLASS
        )
    elif (
        inspect.isfunction(attr)
        or inspect.ismethod(attr)
        or inspect.isbuiltin(attr)
        or isinstance(attr, method_descriptor)
    ):

        # act as functions, let's treat them as functions.
        return AttrCategory.FUNCTION

            AttrCategory.DESCRIPTOR,
            AttrCategory.STATIC_METHOD,

def attr_category_postprocess(get_attr_category_func):
    """Unifies attr_category to a tuple, add AttrCategory.SLOT if needed."""
    @functools.wraps(get_attr_category_func)
    def wrapped(
        name: str, attr: Any, obj: Any
    ) -> Tuple[AttrCategory, ...]:
        category = get_attr_category_func(name, attr, obj)
        category = list(category) if isinstance(category, tuple) else [category]
        if is_slotted_attr(obj, name):
            # Refactoring all tuples to lists is not easy
            # and pleasant. Maybe do this in future if necessary
            category.append(AttrCategory.SLOT)
        return tuple(category)

    return wrapped


@attr_category_postprocess
def get_attr_category(
    name: str, attr: Any, obj: Any
) -> Union[Tuple[AttrCategory, ...], AttrCategory]:
    def is_descriptor(obj: Any) -> bool:
        return (
            hasattr(obj, '__get__')
            or hasattr(obj, '__set__')
            or hasattr(obj, '__delete__')
        )

    method_descriptor = type(list.append)

    if name in ATTR_MAP_CONDITIONAL:
        return ATTR_MAP_CONDITIONAL[name](obj)

    if name in ATTR_MAP:
        return ATTR_MAP[name]

    if inspect.isclass(attr):
        return (
            AttrCategory.EXCEPTION
            if issubclass(attr, Exception)
            else AttrCategory.CLASS
        )
    elif (
        inspect.isfunction(attr)
        or inspect.ismethod(attr)
        or inspect.isbuiltin(attr)
        or isinstance(attr, method_descriptor)
    ):
        # Technically, method_descriptor is descriptor, but since they
        # act as functions, let's treat them as functions.
        return AttrCategory.FUNCTION
    elif isinstance(attr, staticmethod):
        return (
            AttrCategory.DESCRIPTOR,
            AttrCategory.STATIC_METHOD,
            AttrCategory.FUNCTION,
        )
    elif is_descriptor(attr):
        # Maybe add getsetdescriptor memberdescriptor in the future.
        return AttrCategory.DESCRIPTOR, AttrCategory.PROPERTY
    else:
        # attr that is neither function nor class is a normal variable,
        # and it's classified to property.
        return AttrCategory.PROPERTY

def attr_category_postprocess(get_attr_category_func):
    """Unifies attr_category to a tuple, add AttrCategory.SLOT if needed."""
    @functools.wraps(get_attr_category_func)
    def wrapped(
        name: str, attr: Any, obj: Any
    ) -> Tuple[AttrCategory, ...]:
        category = get_attr_category_func(name, attr, obj)
        category = list(category) if isinstance(category, tuple) else [category]
        if is_slotted_attr(obj, name):
            # Refactoring all tuples to lists is not easy
            # and pleasant. Maybe do this in future if necessary
            category.append(AttrCategory.SLOT)
        return tuple(category)

    return wrapped


@attr_category_postprocess
def get_attr_category(
    name: str, attr: Any, obj: Any
) -> Union[Tuple[AttrCategory, ...], AttrCategory]:
    def is_descriptor(obj: Any) -> bool:
        return (
            hasattr(obj, '__get__')
            or hasattr(obj, '__set__')
            or hasattr(obj, '__delete__')
        )

    method_descriptor = type(list.append)

    if name in ATTR_MAP_CONDITIONAL:
        return ATTR_MAP_CONDITIONAL[name](obj)

    if name in ATTR_MAP:
        return ATTR_MAP[name]

    if inspect.isclass(attr):
        return (
            AttrCategory.EXCEPTION
            if issubclass(attr, Exception)
            else AttrCategory.CLASS
        )
    elif (
        inspect.isfunction(attr)
        or inspect.ismethod(attr)
        or inspect.isbuiltin(attr)
        or isinstance(attr, method_descriptor)
    ):
        # Technically, method_descriptor is descriptor, but since they
        # act as functions, let's treat them as functions.
        return AttrCategory.FUNCTION
    elif isinstance(attr, staticmethod):
        return (
            AttrCategory.DESCRIPTOR,
            AttrCategory.STATIC_METHOD,
            AttrCategory.FUNCTION,
        )
    elif is_descriptor(attr):
        # Maybe add getsetdescriptor memberdescriptor in the future.
        return AttrCategory.DESCRIPTOR, AttrCategory.PROPERTY
    else:
        # attr that is neither function nor class is a normal variable,
        # and it's classified to property.
        return AttrCategory.PROPERTY
